hypotheses: Gossypetin, a hexahydroxyflavone, may perturb histone methylation/acetylation states in A375 through flavonoid-mediated chromatin-modifying enzyme inhibition, with the strongest anchor signal being H3K27me1K36me2 loss and H3K56me0 gain.

Structurally related polyphenols/flavonoids such as Exifone, Ginkgetin, curcumin, and Resveratrol may share enough chromatin-response context to serve as transfer donors despite low structure similarity.

Flavopiridol, as a flavonoid-derived CDK inhibitor, may produce a reproducible histone perturbation via transcriptional/CDK-dependent chromatin effects, but its negative anchor similarity makes it a lower-priority donor.
object.evidence_gap: No donor has both high anchor similarity and high structure similarity to gossypetin; the candidate list lacks direct histone-mark response values for gossypetin or matched A375 flavonoid perturbations, so donor selection relies on inferred pharmacological/structural relatedness rather than measured transfer responses.
